_meta.name: Held-out golden sample (seed 123) for the obligations-draft extractor
_meta.method: 40 sentences/points drawn with random.Random(123).sample from the pool of 544 plain-line sentences and marker-less-lead-in points of the non-skipped AMLR articles (same splitting logic as the extractor; list points folded into a marker-bearing lead-in are not pool items). Drawn AFTER the extractor rules were frozen against the development samples (tests/golden/obligations_draft_dev.json seed 7 and obligations_draft_dev2.json seed 99; two rounds of rule fixes: carve-outs, rulemaking and permission rules), and labelled by hand before comparing with extractor output; no rule was changed after seeing these labels. One labeller (the builder, an AI, not a lawyer): NOT an independent legal label. Labelling question: does this sentence or point, read alone, state a duty or prohibition on an identifiable actor? NO for: definitions, scope or allocation rules, deeming rules, permissions ('may', 'shall be permitted'), list points that only complete a lead-in, rulemaking and designation mandates (RTS, guidelines, delegated or implementing acts and their timing, AMLA reviewing standards), and text fragments. 'binds' = the actor the duty falls on (null = ambiguous, not scored).
